chunks: Abū ‘Abdillāh Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Ya’qūb ibn Isḥāq ibn ‘Ammār narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Faḍḍāl, from Muḥammad ibn Walīd, from Yūnus ibn Ya’qūb, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: O Yūnus! On the night of the fifteenth of Sha‘bān, Allāh will forgive every believer who goes to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) all of their past and future sins, and they will be told, 'Go toward (committing) good deeds.' I said, 'Is all of this for those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) on the fifteenth of Sha‘bān?' He said, 'O Yūnus! If I told people about what is given to those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) on this night, the males of the men would travel riding on wood (placed on the back of saddleless camels).'

key_terms.الْخُشُبِ: Wood (referring to the wooden planks placed on saddleless camels for riding)
key_terms.زَارَ الْحُسَيْنَ: Visited Imam Husain (pilgrimage to his shrine)
key_terms.لَيْلَةَ النِّصْفِ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ: The night of the fifteenth of the month of Sha'ban

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husain on the 15th of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the unique spiritual status of Imam Ḥusain (a.s.) as an intercessor on Laylat al-Nisf min Sha'ban, a night traditionally associated with divine decree and forgiveness. The Imam’s remark that men would 'stand on their tiptoes' (or climb trees) illustrates the overwhelming eagerness of the faithful to seize this opportunity for comprehensive absolution, linking the physical act of pilgrimage to profound metaphysical grace.
